brief: Legs B is next, and today, 25 November, is the first day of the lighter week (to 1 December): fewer sets, about 20 percent lighter, nothing hard. Pull B on 24 November went well: row 60 for 10 on all four, close-grip pulldown 135 for 10 on all three (the card asked 9 on the last two), straight-arm pulldown 52.5 for 11, reverse curl 37.5 for 11, curl 30 for 10, face pulls 32.5 for 15, and the first neck set, 10 lb for 15 and 15 on the lying extension. The shrug was 80 for 18 on three sets, the fourth set missing on three of the last four Pull B nights (it was also your longest night at 71 minutes, with the new neck lift after it), so the program is now version 17 and the shrug is three sets, which I said would happen if the fourth set was missing again; write a note on that card if you want the fourth back. Nothing else changed. Tonight's Legs B at lighter-week weights, two sets each: barbell RDL 140 for 8, leg extension 120 for 10, leg press 160 for 10, leg curl 120 for 10, ab wheel 10 reps (one set is enough), ab crunch machine 50 for 10, calf press 240 for 12. Stop every set with plenty left. After the lighter week the numbers go back up: RDL 185 for 10, leg press 200 for 12, leg extension and leg curl 157.5 for 11, calf press 300 for 14. Dates: lighter week to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, show 1 March, 96 days away. Two things I still need: a morning bodyweight (nothing logged since 23 August, 207 lb, 94 days; the Bodyweight button on the workout screen), and your answer on a second calf lift (smith machine or single-leg dumbbell raise off a step) before the 2 December review.

flags.note: The lighter week runs 25 November to 1 December by the calendar: about 60 percent of the sets, weights about 20 percent lighter, nothing near failure.
Program version 17: the dumbbell shrug goes from four sets to three on Pull B (three of four sets done on three of the last four Pull B nights). Pull B is 21 sets.
First neck set logged on 24 November (lying plate neck extension, 10 lb for 15, 15, no note after). Neck flexion on Push A has not been logged yet.
No bodyweight logged since 23 August (207 lb), 94 days ago; prep starts 9 December and needs a starting number.
Calves stay at three sets a day until the 2 December review; a second calf lift needs your answer on equipment you have at your gym.

block.why: Today, 25 November, is the first day of the lighter week (25 November to 1 December): the calendar sets about 60 percent of the usual sets and weights about 20 percent lighter, nothing near failure, then assessment 2 to 8 December and prep from 9 December. The show is 96 days away. Pull B on 24 November closed the build block with every lift on it at or above the card except one: the shrug did three of four sets again (80 for 18, the fourth set missing on three of the last four Pull B nights), so version 17 drops it to three sets and Pull B goes from 22 to 21 sets. The first neck set was logged (10 lb for 15, 15 on the lying extension). The lighter week asks for no more than Legs B tonight, then Push A, Pull A, Legs A: the block is over, the calendar moves on whether or not those are trained, and I am making no other structural change this week. Programming that is left to decide has a date: side delts on 1 December, calves on 2 December, both after the lighter week gives one more Push A and the lighter sessions to read. Loads to beat into assessment: shoulder press 50, chest press 165, row 60 for 10, close pulldown 135 for 10, shrug 80 for 18, lateral raise 17.5, RDL 185, leg press 220, leg extension and leg curl 157.5, calf press 300. Attendance: nine training days in a row from 9 to 17 November, then no log from 18 to 22 November (I do not know why: travel, tiredness and illness would each change what I do, and it is not in your notes), then Push B and Pull B on 23 and 24 November, all at or above card. The lighter week comes by the calendar, not because the logs call for it, and I am leaving it as planned.

chest.why: Eighteen sets a week, inside 12 to 20; seven are aimed at the upper chest (smith incline 4, low-to-high crossover 3). Push B on 23 November: chest press 165 for 10, 10, 10, the top of Push B's 8 to 10 on every set, up from 165 for 9 on 12 November, and high-to-low crossover 30.5 for 15, 15. Push A lifts repeat from 15 November: chest press 157.5 for 12, 12, 12, smith incline 180 for 6, 7, 8, low-to-high crossover 12.5 for 15 on all three. All going up at this gym. Sets hold; the weights move. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 18 planned a week, of which 18 are direct sets; 10.3 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

front-delts.why: Fifteen counted, inside 6 to 16. Eight are the two presses that lead each push day (smith incline 4, shoulder press 4); seven are half credit from the chest press, crossovers and dips. No set is in the week only for front delts, so the only way to lower this is to cut chest or shoulder pressing, and neither should be cut. Shoulder press 50 for 10 on all four sets on 23 November, the first time the top of the range was hit on every set; smith incline 180 for 6, 7, 8 on 15 November. Hold. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 15 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 9.1 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

side-delts.why: Raised on 18 November (version 14). Side delts decide how wide the shoulders look on stage; they had the smallest share of any scored muscle (6 direct sets, 8 counted, against 15.5 for rear delts), so lateral raises went to four sets on each push day: 8 direct, 10 counted with half credit from the shoulder press, the bottom of the 10 to 20 range. First four-set night, 23 November on Push B: 17.5 for 13, 13, 13 and the fourth set was not done, and you asked why four sets for a small muscle. The honest count: the 6.3 a week done is an average over weeks that include rest days and a partial week (the week of 17 to 22 November had no push night) and mostly predate the four-set cards, so it does not prove the fourth set is the problem; there has been exactly one four-set night and three of four sets were done. Direct sets are now 8 against the rear delts' 7; on the counted number it is 10 against 12.5. 15 November on Push A was 17.5 for 12, 12, 12 (three sets, before the fourth existed). The weight is right (17.5, up from 15). The decision between a third lateral day and a second side-delt lift stays with the review of 1 December: the lighter week (25 November to 1 December) cuts sets and is a poor week to add a day, and adding a day now would walk back the 14 November removal of the Pull A cable lateral raise (version 12) inside the 14-day guard. Honest limit on the date: the lighter week runs about 60 percent of the sets at lighter weights, so its Push A cannot show whether a fourth lateral set at 17.5 works. What 1 December adds is calendar, not new evidence: it is the first review with no deload ahead, and the decision (a third lateral day or a second side-delt lift) is made then on the 23 November night and whatever Push A shows. Until then side delts stay at 8 direct, 10 counted, the floor of their range. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 10 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 6.3 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

rear-delts.why: Cut on 18 November (version 14), now held. 7 direct sets (reverse pec deck 3 on Push B, face pulls 2 on each pull day) and 12.5 counted, inside 6 to 14. Reverse pec deck 97.5 for 13, 13, 13 on 23 November, up from 12, 12, 12; weight holds, reps climb to 15 on all three, which earns the next weight. Face pulls 32.5 for 15, 15 on 24 November. Hold. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 12.5 planned a week, of which 7 are direct sets; 10.9 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

The seated row has four sets because the two rows are the only work aimed at back thickness, and 8 direct sets is under the 10 floor, so this is the one place where the direct count is the honest one and I am saying so. Both rows are going up: seated row 112.5 for 10 on all four on 16 November, chest-supported row 60 for 10 on all four on 24 November (9 on 13 November). Hold. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 18 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 13.9 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

calves.why: Nine counted, inside 8 to 16 and near its bottom: six direct sets (the calf press on the leg press, three on each leg day) and three from half credit on the leg curl. On 17 November all three sets were done, 300 for 13, 13, 13, after 300 for 12, 12, 12 on 14 November. On 19 November I asked whether the New York gym has a standing or seated calf machine. I should not have, because your photos of the whole gym from 23 July answer it. There is neither; calf raises are done on the leg press. That question is withdrawn. More calf work would mean a second calf lift: a standing calf raise on the smith machine, or a single-leg dumbbell calf raise off a step platform. That would mean more than three calf sets on a leg day, and three a day is the count you settled in July and August. I will not go past that on my own. So I am asking: do you want calves raised above three sets a day? Until you say, calves stay as they are. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 9 planned a week, of which 6 are direct sets; 4.9 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

neck.why: Raised on 19 November (version 15) from nothing, after you wrote on 18 November that the program had no neck work. The extension was logged for the first time on 24 November: 10 lb for 15, 15, no note after. That is 4 direct sets a week, the bottom of 4 to 12, because a neck is brought up light and for reps. Once each lift has run twice with all reps done and no neck pain, the next step is a second set day for each, toward 8 a week. The four-week average of 0.5 is that one night. Hold; the next step waits for two clean runs of each. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 4 planned a week, of which 4 are direct sets; 0.5 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

prep.plan: About two weeks come before prep (14 days from 25 November). The build block ended on 24 November. This week, 25 November to 1 December, is the lighter week: the calendar sets it at about 60 percent of the usual sets with weights about 20 percent lighter, and nothing taken near failure. The week of 2 December is assessment: each main lift is run at its current weight for its best reps, and the starting bodyweight is set. Prep starts on 9 December and runs just under 12 weeks. Weeks 1 to 4 (9 December to 5 January): the same lifts and weights as now, with the sets as they stand after the side-delt decision (1 December review) and your answer on calves; in prep, holding reps at the same weight while bodyweight comes down is the win. Weeks 5 to 8 (6 January to 2 February): the weights stay, and if recovery slips, sets come off what the stage scores least (rear delts, forearms, traps, the hip machines) before anything comes off side delts, back, chest, arms, quads or calves. Weeks 9 to 11 (3 to 21 February): the same, no new lifts, no set taken to a grinding rep. The final week (22 February to 1 March): about half the sets, with the last hard leg session early in the week. Fat loss is paced at about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, which at your last logged 207 lb is about 1 to 2 lb a week. It is checked by the weekly average of morning weigh-ins: less than half a percent for two weeks running means food or daily walking has to change; more than one percent with reps dropping means it is too fast. From 9 December to the show is just under 12 weeks, so at that pace the most that can come off is roughly 12 to 23 lb from 207. Whether that is enough is not something I can tell: the last weigh-in in the log is 23 August, and there are no photos and no division. If more than that has to come off, the only slack is the 14 days before 9 December, which is why the weigh-in matters this week and not in December. The prep phase in the calendar is a placeholder that detailed programming replaces at assessment, so this plan is a default, not a decision. What it protects, in order, once real data arrives: side delts, upper chest (Push A), back, arms, quads, calves; the deadlift and RDL are climbing 5 to 10 lb a visit now (deadlift 250 for 5 on 16 November) and in a deficit they hold their weight rather than climb. If no bodyweight arrives by 2 December, I will start prep on 9 December from 207 lb (23 August) and say so.

deferred.why: Side delts planned at 10 counted sets (the floor of 10 to 20) but done at 6.3 a week on average over the last four weeks. The next step (a third lateral day or a second side-delt lift) is decided at the 1 December review, after the lighter week, by which point one more Push A and the lighter-week sessions are logged. Adding a day now would walk back the 14 November removal of the Pull A cable lateral raise (version 12) inside the 14-day guard and land in a week that runs fewer sets; waiting is right because the block needs the fourth set logged before more is piled on it.

Calves sit at 9 counted sets and 6 direct, near the bottom of their range, and they are scored on stage. Your gym has no calf machine (your 23 July photos), so adding calf work means a second calf lift (a standing calf raise on the smith machine, or a single-leg dumbbell calf raise off a step), which would take a leg day past the three calf sets you settled in July and August. That is your decision, not mine: it waits for your answer. The 2 December review, at assessment week, is the last point to add it before prep starts on 9 December; if you have not answered by then, calves stay at three sets a day and the review says so.
